A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CAML and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A.1–A.6. Corresponding material can be matched reliably despite added experiments and shifted pagination.

before.justification: v2 reports original driving experiments using AUTOCASTSIM and semantic-segmentation experiments using real-world CoPeD data, including baseline comparisons, ablations, and efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds driving experiments on additional training modalities, LiDAR-only inference, and late cooperation.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A.5 retain the same feature aggregation, multimodal fusion, teacher–student procedure, and distillation objective. The new sensor configurations instantiate the existing general framework; late cooperation is an added comparator rather than a replacement CAML procedure.

E1.justification: The three AUTOCASTSIM traffic scenarios and CoPeD indoor/outdoor segmentation tasks remain. Coverage expands modestly through vehicle-state information used during training and a LiDAR-only CAML inference condition in the new driving analyses.

E2.justification: v3 adds an evaluated late-cooperation baseline in Section 4.1 and Table 5, combining action logits rather than intermediate features. The existing AML, COOPERNAUT, STGN, FCN, teacher, RGB-only BC, and Pre-fusion CAML comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The added experiments vary training modality count and the retained inference modality. The late-cooperation comparison explicitly matches CAML's encoders and distillation procedure while varying cooperation stage. Existing splits, evaluation metrics, and reported training budgets are unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 3–5 substantially expand the driving ablations to address three previously untested questions: the value of additional state information, the choice of retained sensor, and intermediate versus late cooperation. These complement the retained teacher/RGB-only BC ablation, agent-count generalization test, and segmentation fusion-order analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions specify four repeated runs with means and standard deviations in Section 4.1. The added driving tables continue that reporting practice. Appendix A.6's new uncertainty-estimation discussion concerns future work, not an implemented statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Matched original results remain unchanged. New Tables 3–5 report, for example, left-turn ADR of 69.7±1.2 with state-augmented training, 68.0±0.9 with LiDAR-only inference, and 60.2±1.3 for late cooperation, alongside standard CAML's retained 67.3±1.0. These are additional configurations and comparator results.

T1.justification: The mathematical problem formulation, centralized/decentralized complexity analysis, Appendix A.1 coverage and mutual-information reasoning, and Appendix A.5 loss equations are retained. No new theorem, proof, derivation, or formal definition is introduced.

C1.justification: v3 adds an explicit qualified priority claim that CAML is the first flexible, principled framework for multimodal multi-agent inference with limited modalities. The introduction also emphasizes cross-agent knowledge transfer and team-level coordination. The principal contributions and headline performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 attributes LiDAR-only performance to spatial localization and the late-cooperation deficit to information loss from output-level fusion. Appendix A.6 retains the proposed modality-dropout direction but removes the explicit reliable-communication assumption and communication-failure caveat, replacing them with proposed uncertainty estimation for noisy or degraded sensors.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 documents the new late-cooperation implementation: ResNet-18 and Point Transformer encoders, MLP action heads, intervehicle logit averaging, subsequent modality fusion, and the matched distillation procedure. Existing appendix disclosures of hardware, optimizer, training duration, and distillation hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references concerning multimodal reasoning, robotic feeding, robust control, and uncertainty-aware distillation, while removing the Bayoudh survey and Zhuang perception-fusion reference. Related-work discussion adds dynamic-team challenges and AUKT, but retains the existing collaboration, AML, and distillation organization.

P1.justification: Selected introduction and related-work paragraphs are revised, Appendix A.6 is rewritten, and Section 3 gains 'Problem Formulation' and 'Approach' labels. Author information is reformatted and an acknowledgment is added. Most prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds three compact tables for the new driving analyses. The original segmentation Table 3 becomes Table 6, appendix Tables 4–5 become Tables 7–8, and some displays shift position. All seven figures retain identical image content; the overall visual format remains similar.

improvement.justification: Tables 3–5 provide useful additional evidence for modality flexibility and the choice of intermediate cooperation, strengthening validation beyond v2's existing comparisons. This modest benefit is partly offset by Appendix A.6's removal of the explicit communication-reliability limitation. The added diagnostic evidence supports a limited net improvement while the core method, theory, and original benchmark findings remain unchanged.
